newsitem.title: USA: Ohio soft red winter wheat ratings improve a bit.
newsitem.headline: Ohio soft red winter wheat ratings improve a bit.

text.p: Ohio's winter wheat improved slightly and was rated 50 percent good to excellent versus 46 last week in the week ended Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop report.
Wheat was rated four percent very poor and 13 percent poor, the same as last week. Thirty-three percent was rated fair and 50 percent good to excellent.
"Farmers continued to prepare fields for planting as 4.6 days were considered suitable for fieldwork during the seven-day period which ended Friday, April 11," the report said.
The soil temperature in Ohio is still considered too cold to plant corn. Only two percent of the corn crop has been planted, compared to one percent last year and a five-year average of nil.
Topsoil was rated 10 percent short, 77 percent adequate and 13 percent surplus.
Pasture condition improved slightly and was rated 50 percent good to excellent, 37 percent fair, 10 percent poor and three percent very poor.
